title: Data is all you need: Finetuning LLMs for Chip Design via an Automated design-data augmentation framework
problem: Insufficient Verilog training data and lack of automated data augmentation framework hinder LLM-based hardware description language generation, significantly increasing the time required to prepare training datasets.
motivation: Large language models show promise for automated chip design through HDL code generation, but need high-quality training data to improve code generation quality.
method: The framework automatically creates training datasets in three ways: translating Verilog (chip design code) into descriptions of how it's structured and what each part does, using templates; deliberately introducing errors into working code and pairing them with feedback from design tools to create repair examples; and using GPT-3.5 to generate descriptions of design automation scripts. These synthetic training pairs teach Llama2 models (13B and 7B parameter versions) how to generate Verilog code.
key_novelty: The framework automatically generates abundant training data by pairing Verilog code with natural language explanations and repair examples, using code-structure analysis and design tool feedback.
contributions: Automated data augmentation framework for Verilog and EDA script generation
Template-based AST-to-natural-language translation for synthesizing Verilog descriptions
EDA-feedback-driven mechanism for generating Verilog repair training pairs
ChipGPT-FT1 model achieving 70.6% accuracy in Verilog generation, outperforming prior SOTA open-source models

metrics.other: Pass rate improvement over GPT-3.5; effective EDA script generation with 200 training examples

limitations: Limitations not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Data augmentation for LLM-based automated chip design
